summary:
US President Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller, his most trusted adviser and the architect of his immigration crackdown, as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, who is stepping down. Democratic and Republican lawmakers have criticised the appointment, with Democrats calling Miller a 'hatemonger' and a 'xenophobe'. The appointment follows a Democratic blue wave in the midterm elections, and Democratic lawmakers say they will prioritise the cost of living, alleged corruption and tighter oversight of ICE agents.

Paraguay's Congress impeached President Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, and he was placed under house arrest minutes later. Vice President Pedro Alliana became president on Friday. Reports differ on how many people are affected: one says 60% of the country cannot access accounts, while another says nearly half of Paraguayans are locked out of their savings.

Dozens of European flights were disrupted by bomb threats this week, and at least 18 more were affected on Friday. Searches found no explosive devices. The Irish government said the hoaxes were likely a coordinated campaign of disruption.

headlines.title: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff
headlines.summary: Trump has appointed Stephen Miller, his most trusted adviser and architect of the immigration crackdown, to replace Susie Wiles, who is stepping down. Democratic and Republican lawmakers criticised the appointment, with Democrats calling Miller a 'hatemonger' and a 'xenophobe'.

headlines.title: Democrats win US midterm elections in blue wave
headlines.summary: Democrats won the US midterm elections in a blue wave, and Democratic lawmakers say they will prioritise the rising cost of living, alleged corruption and tighter oversight of ICE agents. Asian and European stock markets fell sharply on Friday after a rout in US tech stocks, with analysts citing big worries over AI.

headlines.title: Paraguay's president removed and placed under house arrest
headlines.summary: Paraguay's Congress impeached President Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, and he was placed under house arrest minutes later. Vice President Pedro Alliana became president on Friday, and the number of people locked out of their accounts is given as 60% of the country in one report and nearly half of Paraguayans in another.

headlines.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights and media across Europe
headlines.summary: Dozens of European flights were disrupted by bomb threats this week, and at least 18 more flights were affected on Friday. Searches found no explosive devices, and the Irish government said the hoaxes were likely a coordinated campaign of disruption.

headlines.title: Pope Leo begins 12-day South America tour in Uruguay
headlines.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay on Friday at the start of a 12-day tour that also includes Argentina and Peru, three weeks after lung surgery. He called for healthcare to be accessible to all.

headlines.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years
headlines.summary: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the deaths of children starved on his orders. One report puts the number of dead at 191 and describes the sentence as life imprisonment.

headlines.title: New Zealand election too close to call
headlines.summary: New Zealand's election remained too close to call as early results came in, with the National-Luxon coalition and Labour neck-and-neck. Polls show no coalition is expected to win a majority of seats, and a minor party is cast as kingmaker.
